note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in fingers and pain in right wrist.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a landscaper presenting with several months of right wrist and hand pain associated with numbness and tingling. Symptoms began insidiously without identified trigger. Patient notes symptoms are worse at night, often waking with hand asleep requiring shaking out. Numbness affects all fingers but is more prominent in thumb and index finger, with occasional involvement of fifth finger. Associated with grip weakness and dropping objects due to difficulty feeling items. Patient denies similar symptoms in right hand. Occupational history significant for heavy repetitive labor including raking and digging as part of landscaping work.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies right hand involvement. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in landscaping doing yard work and maintenance. Reports heavy labor with repetitive motions on a daily basis. Alcohol use: beer or two on Friday and Saturday weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Cardiovascular and lungs auscultated without abnormality. Grip strength decreased on left compared to right. Sensation intact to touch on right side fingers, slightly diminished on thumb compared to pointer finger. Bilateral positive Tinel's sign elicited on wrist percussion.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome. Plan includes: activity modification with delegation of heavy repetitive tasks to other employees for several weeks, wrist splint, ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours. EMG study ordered to measure electrical impulses. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Will assess need for further diagnostic testing or possible surgical intervention at that time.
